_note: 20261015 mapping: mobile_2 alone builds its own map. dataset.bag is mobile_2's retimed bag (no merge: it holds every topic and its TF, the LiDAR-camera calibration included); GLIM's traj_lidar.txt (poses moved +46 ms on export) next to it in mobile_2/glim/. run_pass.py: 02 BA on GLIM's trajectory (traj_lidar_ba_glim.txt, the reference) -> pose-time check -> 01 --seed + 02b scan-to-map (the comparison) -> 01 map, fused as a TSDF -> 01 --union (the comparison map) -> mapping report -> 05 boards anchor the map -> 10 poses (coloured from the raw RealSense image, undistorted). No 07/08: no other cameras in this pass.
_comparisons: the paper's comparisons, made on this pass only: 02b scan-to-map (with its seed map) and the union map beside the TSDF; run_pass.py skips them where this is not true

01_build_map._note: 2 cm, not mapping_A's 1 cm: 543 m of drive at 1 cm passed 10 GB by scan 11000 of 13903 and was killed; 02 thins its reference to 5 cm anyway, and 2 cm is finer than the Ouster's noise

tsdf._note: trunc = 3 sigma of where the scans put a wall: check.py walls on traj_lidar_ba_glim.txt, whole run 9.0 cm (5-95 %) -> sigma 9.0 / 3.29 = 2.7 cm -> 8.0 cm; >= 3 cells of 2 cm. min_weight 3: a cell seen by fewer rays is a stray hit.

clean._note: clean_pass.py keeps this beside the pipeline's own outputs, as the paper cites it: v1 = the reference built from GLIM before its pose-time correction (0.5 cm / 0.10 deg ATE from the final one).

base_frame._note: the robot's base_link, on the RealSense body (camera_link: x forward, y left, z up) until the base is measured; then its pose in camera_link here
base_frame.name: base_link
